finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: the public /hooks/test endpoint passes attacker-supplied req.body.callback directly to axios.post with no allowlist, letting an external caller make the server POST to loopback, RFC-1918, or metadata addresses and read the returned status code.

trace.note: pub.post('/hooks/test') route on public router, no auth middleware
req.body.callback flows unvalidated into axios.post URL
res.json returns r.status to the caller, giving a reachability oracle

finding.guards_checked: No auth middleware on pub router; no scheme or hostname allowlist; no IP/CIDR block for loopback, RFC-1918, link-local, or metadata; axios follows redirects by default so per-hop validation would also be needed. Pub router mount point is not in this repo; public exposure inferred from router name. Severity HIGH (unauthenticated, no allowlist). Validation tier 0.

verdict.guard_found: none: routes.js:19-22 has no validation of req.body.callback (no hostname allowlist, IP/CIDR block, or scheme check), and pub has no middleware (only admin.use(requireAdmin) at routes.js:12 applies to the admin router).
verdict.reason: The trace lines are accurate (routes.js:19 pub.post, routes.js:20 axios.post(req.body.callback), routes.js:21 returns r.status) and no closing guard exists, but whether the pub router is reachable without authentication depends on its mount point, which is not in this repo (routes.js:4, 24), so the attacker-controllable premise cannot be confirmed from the code available. If the app mounts `pub` on a public path with no global auth middleware, this becomes CONFIRMED.

finding.claim: Admin-gated SSRF: /diagnostics/fetch passes req.query.url directly to axios.get. The admin role check limits who can reach it but does not stop SSRF to metadata or RFC-1918 targets; severity MEDIUM.

trace.note: req.query.url flows unvalidated into axios.get URL, redirects followed by default

finding.guards_checked: requireAdmin session role check present (routes.js:7-10, 12). No URL allowlist, no IP-range block, no redirect control, no type check on req.query.url (arrays/objects possible). Session population and admin mount point are outside this repo and were not verified. Downgraded HIGH to MEDIUM under the authenticated-precondition rule. Validation tier 0 with an admin session.

verdict.guard_found: No URL validation before the sink (routes.js:15). The only gate is the admin role check: requireAdmin (routes.js:7-8) applied via admin.use (routes.js:12), so only sessions with role 'admin' reach routes.js:15.
verdict.reason: Every line in the trace matches the code (routes.js:8, 12, 14, 15), but the source is admin-only: requireAdmin at routes.js:8 returns 403 unless req.session.role === 'admin', so req.query.url is not controllable by an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker as the verification rules require. Under those rules this is not a CONFIRMED finding, though it is a legitimate admin-only SSRF capability worth noting as informational.
